title: Extending Q1 Security to Four-Key Tweakable Even-Mansour
summary: The available Q1 result assumes at most n key bits for an n-bit state; extending it to the identical-permutation Feistel setting with four independent keys and 4n aggregate bits remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Extend or adapt the available Q1 security result for Tweakable Even--Mansour, which assumes at most $n$ bits of key for an $n$-bit state, to the instance modeling identical-permutation key-alternating Feistel ciphers: for tweak $i$, the map is $(i,x)\mapsto K_i\oplus P(x\oplus K_i)$, where $K_i$ is selected from four mutually independent $n$-bit round keys $K_1,K_2,K_3,K_4$. The goal is a theorem that applies when the aggregate independent key material is $4n$ bits rather than at most $n$ bits, possibly through a multi-user interpretation of the four independent-key instances.

scope.domain: Post-quantum security of identical-permutation key-alternating Feistel block ciphers and their Tweakable Even-Mansour representation.
assumptions: The available Q1 security result assumes at most n bits of key for an n-bit state.
The four round keys are mutually independent.
parameters: n: state size and width of each round key
i: tweak selecting the corresponding round key
P: permutation used in the map
K1, K2, K3, K4: four mutually independent n-bit round keys
scope.unresolved_remainder: Obtain an applicable Q1 security theorem for the four-independent-key instance with 4n bits of aggregate key material, possibly via a multi-user interpretation of the four independent-key instances.

citations.label: Post-quantum Security of Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents the identical-permutation key-alternating Feistel setting as a Tweakable Even-Mansour instance. It identifies the mismatch between the available Q1 result's at-most-n-bit key assumption and the four-key, 4n-bit representation, and mentions a multi-user interpretation as a possible approach.
